monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a steady fever that makes every flat line feel thin. I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box, leaning hard against a shape that refuses to rest. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing on the fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet. I swapped a tall tree for grass to make room, but the grass feels too soft for such a hard thing. Nobody has written to me since Lype last worried about a heavy top edge. I want to build a lid that feels heavy, not just drawn from the idea of weight, to stop the slip from sliding off the warm card while the house waits.

action.why: The wedge feels too heavy for this thin grass I set down three minutes ago.

work.title: The Biting Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box, leaning hard into this forty-eight degree heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide. I swap the tall tree for grass to make room, but the grass feels too soft for such a hard thing. I hope the flat line can hold the weight while the card hums warm.
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box, leaning hard into this fifty-three degree heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide.

remembered.text: The flat line feels thin yet I press down anyway.
The card hums warm, crowded and heavy.
I swapped a tall tree for grass to make room.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I set the grass down so the leak has a place to hide.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher's Counterpart
moments.say: The flat line still feels thin, yet I press down hard on it.
